title: Earwax: Live With It
summary: Josh and Chuck explore earwax (cerumen): what it is (secretions of sebaceous and apocrine glands mixed with dead skin, hair, and debris), why ethnic/genetic differences produce wet versus dry earwax (ABCC11 gene), and its four functions: acidic environment against bacteria and fungus, lubrication, trapping debris, and carrying junk out of the ear via jaw movement. They cover problems from cotton swab use, impaction, swimmer's ear, and home remedies like mineral oil and irrigation, then debunk ear candling (auricular candling, coning), which claims to create a vacuum to pull out impurities but has been shown not to work, with burn and injury risks and a 2005 fatal fire. The episode closes with listener mail about ice cream follow-up: black cows, vanilla varieties, and cake cones.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke about episode numbering, running out of topics, and whether they have earwax.

segments.title: Wet vs. dry earwax and genetics
segments.summary: Discussion of ethnic differences in earwax type (dry in East Asia, wet elsewhere) and the ABCC11 gene, with recessive dry-wax allele inheritance.

segments.title: What earwax is and how it moves
segments.summary: Earwax (cerumen) is made of sebaceous gland sebum, apocrine gland secretions, keratin, dead skin, hair, and debris, produced in the outer third of the ear canal and moved outward by jaw movement.

segments.title: Four functions of earwax
segments.summary: Earwax creates an acidic environment that fights bacteria and fungus, lubricates the canal, traps dead skin and debris, and carries it out of the ear. Hosts share an anecdote about moisturizing chapped ears and a spider in an ear.

segments.title: Cotton swabs, impaction, and swimmer's ear
segments.summary: Cotton swabs push earwax deeper and can cause impaction, perforation, and swimmer's ear from over-cleaning. Impaction symptoms and doctor treatments such as syringing are described.

segments.title: Home remedies, irrigation, and diabetes caution
segments.summary: Warm mineral oil and peroxide as home remedies; ear irrigation cautions for perforated eardrums and diabetes; advice to clean only the outer ear with a cloth; spending on ear-cleaning products.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Break before the ear candling segment.

segments.title: Ear candling explained
segments.summary: Ear candling (auricular candling, coning) involves a hollow cone placed in the ear and lit, supposedly creating a vacuum to draw out impurities; claimed origins and benefits are listed, including claims from a Discovery expo booth.

segments.title: Debunking ear candling
segments.summary: Ear candles cannot create a vacuum or pass anything through an intact eardrum; residue is candle ash and wax; injuries include burns, perforation, and infection; a 2005 fatal fire is described; manufacturers label kits for entertainment only.

segments.title: Ice cream follow-up listener mail
segments.summary: A listener who works at Wilson's ice cream parlor describes vanilla types and the varying meanings of a black cow; another listener notes cake cones.
